title: Unified declaration surfaces need declared-only derivation and data-layer family defaults
summary: Two review findings: (1) fail-safe/undeclared resolutions are authority signals only — gate every routing derivation on declared. (2) A code prefix shadows ALL data-layer declarations for its family — family defaults belong in the governed overlay when plugins own the family (service:<provider> ops).
reusable_steps: Two review findings: (1) fail-safe/undeclared resolutions are authority signals only — gate every routing derivation on declared
(2) A code prefix shadows ALL data-layer declarations for its family — family defaults belong in the governed overlay when plugins own the family (service:<provider> ops)
expected_outcome: Lessons from MSN-ADMISSION-UNIFY-20261102 review: (1) Declared-only derivation — a fail-safe entry resolved for AUTHORITY must never drive ROUTING; deriving storageChannel from an undeclared external-admission fail-safe silently repartitioned approval storage. Gate: resolved.declared ? derive : undefined. (2) Data-layer family defaults — code prefixes beat every overlay/plugin declaration for their family including exact entries; a code service: prefix would have killed the plugin extension path for service:<provider>:* ops. Family defaults for plugin-owned namespaces belong in the governed overlay where data exact entries still win; the overlay schema grows the same entry fields (protectedPaths, approvalDomain). (3) Bridge-over-flatten — policy systems stay authoritative detail layers behind registered bridges; the registry adds unified lookup, per-axis fail-safes matching each systems own default, and provenance. (4) Pilot via parameter not wrapper — a subject param through the existing creation function migrated all gate callers without touching mocked module surfaces.
